areal_capacitance.note: No areal capacitance reported; electrochemical results are expressed as specific capacitance.

composition.note: Ti3C2Tx is the electrode material; individual termination fractions were not quantified.

current_density.note: Current density for the reported >100 F g-1 H2SO4 value was not stated.

electrode_thickness.note: Shared capillary-cell method: binder-free electrodes were about 2 mm hand-compressed.

electrolyte.note: Best reported specific capacitance was obtained in the reference Swagelok-cell test.

flake_size.note: No numerical lateral flake size was reported in the supplied paper text.

gravimetric_capacitance.note: Reference Swagelok-cell test in Figure S21; stated to exceed 100 F g-1.

interlayer_spacing.note: Working electrode in 1M H2SO4 at 1 V under static charge-equilibrated conditions.

layer_no.note: No numerical layer count or explicit few-layer designation reported for the electrode.

mass_loading.note: Only total typical loading (about 1–2 mg) was given; no areal loading was reported.

mxene_formula.note: Reported throughout the title, abstract, methods, and keywords.

scan_rate.note: No CV scan rate associated with the >100 F g-1 result was stated.

ssa.note: Discussion states the MXene used had BET surface area below 10 m2 g-1.

synthesis_method.note: Ti3AlC2 was etched using LiF plus 12 M HCl at 55 °C for 48 h.

tortuosity.note: No tortuosity value or impedance-model extraction was reported.

summary: The study used one binder-free Ti3C2Tx MXene electrode material, synthesized by LiF/HCl etching of Ti3AlC2, followed by LiCl treatment, HCl washing, and freeze-drying. The same MXene was assembled as symmetric parallel-plate electrodes and evaluated with 1 M H2SO4, LiCl, NaCl, KCl, RbCl, CsCl, and NH4Cl; these electrolyte tests are not separate electrode-material variants. The best explicitly reported capacitance was exceeding 100 F g-1 in a 1 M H2SO4 Swagelok reference cell, with no associated current density stated. The paper does not report areal/volumetric capacitance, areal mass loading, flake size, pore size, porosity, or tortuosity.
